title: Psalms Chapter 105 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 105 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 105 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 105.

questions.question: What should we give unto the LORD according to Psalms 105:1?
questions.explanation: We are instructed to give thanks unto the LORD as stated in Psalms 105:1.

questions.question: What should we do to make known His deeds among the people?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:1 tells us to call upon His name to make known His deeds.

questions.question: According to Psalms 105:3, what should the heart of those who seek the LORD do?
questions.explanation: The verse states that those who seek the LORD should rejoice, as mentioned in Psalms 105:3.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 105:5 encourages us to forget the marvellous works of the LORD.
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:5 instructs us to remember His marvellous works, not to forget them.

questions.question: What does Psalms 105:6 refer to when it mentions 'the seed of Abraham'?
questions.explanation: This verse refers to the children of Jacob as the chosen ones of God, as mentioned in Psalms 105:6.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 105:7 states that the judgments of the LORD are only in Israel.
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:7 indicates that His judgments are in all the earth, not just Israel.

questions.question: What did the LORD remember according to Psalms 105:8?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:8 states that He hath remembered His covenant forever.

questions.question: What did He promise to give to Abraham according to Psalms 105:11?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:11 states that He promised to give the land of Canaan as an inheritance.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 105:12 mentions that Israel was a large nation when they sojourned in Egypt.
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:12 states that they were but a few men in number when they were in Egypt.

questions.question: What did the LORD do to kings for the sake of His people, according to Psalms 105:14?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:14 states that He reproved kings for the sake of His people.

questions.question: What was the condition of Joseph when he was sent before his brothers, as mentioned in Psalms 105:17?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:17 states that Joseph was sold as a servant.

questions.question: In what way did the LORD test Joseph according to Psalms 105:19?
options: By trying him with His word
questions.correctAnswer: By trying him with His word
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:19 mentions that the word of the LORD tried Joseph.

questions.question: What did the LORD do for the Israelites as they departed from Egypt, according to Psalms 105:38?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:38 states that Egypt was glad when they departed because the fear of them fell upon Egypt.

questions.question: In Psalms 105, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:1 is the first instruction given in the chapter.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 105 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 105 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the Lord call for upon the land according to Psalms 105:16?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:16 states, 'Moreover he called for a famine upon the land: he brake the whole staff of bread.' This indicates that God initiated a famine as part of His sovereign plan.

questions.question: Who did God send before His people during the famine as mentioned in Psalms 105:17?
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 105:17, 'He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant,' indicating Joseph's significant role in God's plan.

questions.question: True or False: The king loosed Joseph when he was imprisoned because he was impressed by his wisdom.
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:20 states, 'The king sent and loosed him; even the ruler of the people, and let him go free.' The reason for Joseph's release is not explicitly stated as being due to wisdom, but rather as part of God's plan.

questions.question: According to Psalms 105:21, what position was Joseph made ruler over?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:21 says, 'He made him lord of his house, and ruler of all his substance,' highlighting Joseph's elevation in status.

questions.question: What did God do to the hearts of the Egyptians as stated in Psalms 105:25?
options: Turned them to hate His people
questions.correctAnswer: Turned them to hate His people
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:25 states, 'He turned their heart to hate his people, to deal subtilly with his servants,' illustrating God's control over the hearts of nations.

questions.question: True or False: The signs and wonders shown by Moses and Aaron were in the land of Canaan.
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:27 says, 'They shewed his signs among them, and wonders in the land of Ham,' indicating these events occurred in Egypt, not Canaan.

questions.question: What does Psalms 105:29 say God turned the waters into?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:29 states, 'He turned their waters into blood, and slew their fish,' illustrating one of the plagues God sent upon Egypt.

questions.question: What is the significance of God sending darkness in Psalms 105:28?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:28 states, 'He sent darkness, and made it dark; and they rebelled not against his word,' demonstrating God's authority over nature and His ability to execute judgment.

questions.question: How does Psalms 105:36-37 illustrate God's provision for His people?
options: He brought them forth with silver and gold
questions.correctAnswer: He brought them forth with silver and gold
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:37 states, 'He brought them forth also with silver and gold: and there was not one feeble person among their tribes,' showing God's abundant provision.

questions.question: What lesson can believers learn about obedience from Psalms 105:45?
options: To trust in their own strength
To observe His statutes and keep His laws
questions.correctAnswer: To observe His statutes and keep His laws
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:45 states, 'That they might observe his statutes, and keep his laws,' emphasizing the importance of obedience to God's commands.

questions.question: True or False: The land brought forth frogs in abundance according to Psalms 105:30.
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:30 confirms, 'Their land brought forth frogs in abundance, in the chambers of their kings,' as part of the plagues God sent upon Egypt.

questions.question: What does Psalms 105:16 teach us about God's control over circumstances?
options: He can change events at will
He is limited by human actions
questions.correctAnswer: He can change events at will
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:16 states that God called for a famine, demonstrating His sovereignty and ability to influence circumstances according to His purposes.

questions.question: What is the overarching theme of Psalms 105 regarding God's actions?
questions.explanation: The entire chapter recounts God's faithfulness to His covenant promises, particularly with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, as outlined in verses like Psalms 105:9-10.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 105 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 105.

questions.question: What did the Lord send to the land of Egypt to cause distress according to Psalms 105:31?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'He spake, and there came divers sorts of flies, and lice in all their coasts' (Psalms 105:31), indicating the specific affliction sent by God.

questions.question: Which of the following miracles is NOT mentioned in Psalms 105?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105 recounts various miracles including turning water into blood and opening the rock for water, but does not mention healing the sick.

questions.question: In Psalms 105:37, how did the Lord bring forth His people from Egypt?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'He brought them forth also with silver and gold: and there was not one feeble person among their tribes' (Psalms 105:37), indicating that they left with riches.

questions.question: What did God remember according to Psalms 105:42?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions, 'For he remembered his holy promise, and Abraham his servant' (Psalms 105:42), highlighting God's faithfulness to His promises.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 105:26-27 to emphasize God's actions through Moses and Aaron?
questions.explanation: The verses use parallelism by presenting Moses and Aaron as God's servants, indicating the duality of their roles in the exodus narrative.

questions.question: According to Psalms 105:44, what did God give to His people?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'And gave them the lands of the heathen: and they inherited the labour of the people' (Psalms 105:44), indicating God's provision for Israel.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 105 states that Egypt was glad when the Israelites departed.
questions.explanation: The verse confirms, 'Egypt was glad when they departed: for the fear of them fell upon them' (Psalms 105:38), indicating their relief at the departure of the Israelites.

questions.question: What significant event involving the firstborn is mentioned in Psalms 105:36?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'He smote also all the firstborn in their land, the chief of all their strength' (Psalms 105:36), referring directly to the tenth plague in Egypt.

questions.question: In Psalms 105:40, what did God provide in response to the people's requests?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates, 'The people asked, and he brought quails, and satisfied them with the bread of heaven' (Psalms 105:40), showing God's provision for their needs.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 105 recounts that the Israelites left Egypt with many feeble persons among them.
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:37 states, '...and there was not one feeble person among their tribes,' indicating that they left strong and healthy.

questions.question: Which event in Exodus does Psalms 105:29, turning water into blood, parallel?
options: The crossing of the Red Sea
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:29 states, 'He turned their waters into blood, and slew their fish,' paralleling the first plague in Exodus 7:20-21.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word for 'marvelous' (נִפְלָאִים) in Psalms 105:5 imply about God's works?
questions.explanation: The term implies an element of wonder and awe, indicating that God's works are beyond human understanding, as noted in 'Remember his marvellous works' (Psalms 105:5).

questions.question: In Psalms 105:43, how did God bring forth His people?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'And he brought forth his people with joy, and his chosen with gladness' (Psalms 105:43), indicating a celebratory exodus.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 105 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 105 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 105:1 encourage us to do in relation to the Lord?
options: Give thanks and call upon His name
questions.correctAnswer: Give thanks and call upon His name
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:1 instructs us to give thanks unto the LORD and to call upon His name, emphasizing gratitude and recognition of His deeds.

questions.question: Which covenant is mentioned in Psalms 105:9?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:9 specifies that the covenant made was with Abraham, highlighting God's promise and faithfulness to His chosen people.

questions.question: According to Psalms 105:6, who are referred to as the chosen ones of God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:6 identifies the children of Jacob as His chosen ones, showing God's specific selection of Israel for His purposes.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated in Psalms 105:7 when it states, 'He is the LORD our God'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:7 affirms God's sovereignty over all the earth, indicating His supreme authority and governance.

questions.question: In Psalms 105:16, what did God call for upon the land?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:16 mentions that God called for a famine upon the land, illustrating His control over natural events.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'he brake the whole staff of bread' in Psalms 105:16 imply about the famine?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'he brake the whole staff of bread' in Psalms 105:16 indicates a severe, widespread famine that impacted all.

questions.question: What does Psalms 105:45 suggest is the purpose of God giving the lands of the heathen to His people?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:45 indicates that the purpose of giving the lands of the heathen was to fulfill His promises and allow His people to observe His statutes.

questions.question: According to Psalms 105:22, what role did Joseph play in Egypt?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:22 states that Joseph was made lord of his house and ruler of all his substance, highlighting his elevated status in Egypt.

questions.question: What does Psalms 105:27 indicate about the signs Moses and Aaron performed?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:27 reveals that Moses and Aaron showed God's signs and wonders, indicating their miraculous nature.

questions.question: What does Psalms 105:39 reveal about God's protection over His people during their journey?
options: He spread a cloud for a covering
questions.correctAnswer: He spread a cloud for a covering
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:39 describes how God provided a cloud for covering, signifying His protective presence over His people.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'he opened the rock' in Psalms 105:41 signify?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:41 illustrates God's provision for His people by opening the rock to provide water, demonstrating His care and sustenance.

questions.question: What combined insight do Psalms 105:5 and Psalms 105:7 give regarding God's character?
options: He performs wonders and is just
questions.correctAnswer: He performs wonders and is just
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:5 emphasizes God's marvelous works and judgments, indicating His active involvement and just nature.

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching can be derived from Psalms 105:11 and Psalms 105:36 regarding God's promises?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:11 and Psalms 105:36 together affirm that God's promises, such as the land of Canaan and deliverance, are consistently fulfilled.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not intervene in human history. What does Psalms 105:14-15 actually teach?
options: God is indifferent to our suffering
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:14-15 illustrates that God reproved kings for the sake of His people, demonstrating His active protective intervention in history.
